exposure: Elective induction of labor before 39 weeks
Before and after implementation of a 39 week "hard stop" policy
cohort: 2,574 women who underwent elective induction of labor
finding: Implementation of a "hard stop" policy aimed at eliminating elective inductions before 39 weeks did not affect the rate of cesarean birth but was associated with a decreased rate of postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: Implementing a "hard stop" policy to eliminate elective inductions before 39 weeks did not affect the rate of cesarean birth.
